docs.title: HIVE
docs.text:
Hydrodynamic Identification and Validation Environment

HIVE is a Python framework for wave energy converter (WEC) hydrodynamic modelling, identification, and model benchmarking.

docs.title: What HIVE does
docs.text:
HIVE provides structured pipelines to:

  • Process CFD simulation data
  • Validate existing physics and data-based models against CFD reference data
  • Identify model parameters and data-driven surrogates from CFD reference data

docs.title: Key features
docs.text:
• BEM-based linear and weakly-nonlinear hydrodynamic model
  • Viscous drag identification
  • PI gain identification for PTO control
  • Multiple and various data-based model (wave-to-force-to-velocity state-space, system identification for nonlinear dynamic (SINDY), neural network)
  • model benchmarking through large metric bank

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Depending on the run type the requirements can be:

  • environment surrogate
  • A HydroSphere BEM pickle file (r5_m40.pkl is the project default) placed under source/models/bem/<name_pkl>/<name_pkl>.pkl for validation and/or identification pipeline
  • A reference raw dataset folder placed under 'data/cfd/' for handle pipeline
  • A reference handled dataset (.csv) for validation and identification pipeline placed under data/handled/
  • A model folder with model definition (.json) for validation and/or identification pipeline placed under source/models/

docs.title: Quick start example
docs.text: All scripts are run as modules from inside the code/ folder. A series of tests are available in the test run, and cover HIVE functionality while serving as introduction for users. Here test_0, test_2 and test_9 are quickly introduced to get started. When repeating the test run again, a user command is required, choose [1] erase and redo all. More information is available in the user manual.

docs.title: Handling cfd data (test_0)
docs.text:
The test_0_handle_case.json handle and process a raw CFD simulation (case out_Case_65_20_120000_-430000). It uses a corresponding bem model (r5_m40.pkl) to reconstruct forces. Run it with the command: 

python -m script.run_handle_data --case test_0_handle_case.json

Outputs land in data/handled/test_0_handle_case/. More information is available in the user manual.

As an example, the accumulated absorbed energy time serie is shown below:

docs.title: Validate models (test_2)
docs.text:
This test_2_physics.json validate and compare physics-based WEC models, ranging from full linear to nonlinear FK, against the reference cfd data from test_0. Run it with: 

python -m script.run_validate --case test_2_physics.json

The output data land in out/identified_case/test_2_physics/.

Metrics and plots are then generated by running the corresponding input metric file test_2_metric.json:

python -m script.run_metric --case test_2_metric.json

The scalar metric is shown below:

docs.title: Identify models (test_9)
docs.text:
The test_9_viscous_drag.json identifies a viscous drag for possible method (type) and search type, over the previous CFD case from test_0. Run it with: 

python -m script.run_identify --case test_9_viscous_drag.json

Outputs land in source/models/test_9_viscous_drag/ for identification results. When repeating the test run again, a user command is required, choose [1] erase and redo all. More information is available in the user manual.

docs.title: Metric
docs.text: Metrics computed by run_metric for every model against the reference (CFD case or reference model), per case.

docs.title: Scalar metrics
docs.text:
The scalar metrics are computed on the coarser of the model and reference time grids, within the valid window and the span of both runs. On nested grids (e.g. dt 0.2 vs 0.01) the finer run is then sampled exactly, without interpolation error. The cross-correlation and phase curves stay on the reference grid.

{tag} is one of x, xdot, f_pto, P_abs unless noted. f_pto is the fpto column and P_abs the Pabs column of each run (each run with its own PTO).

Metric key Applies to Formula / Definition Unit nrmse_range_{tag} x, xdot, f_pto, P_abs NRMSE normalised by signal range: RMSE / (max−min) of reference — nrmse_true_{tag} x, xdot, f_pto, P_abs NRMSE normalised by RMS of reference: RMSE / RMS(ref) — rel_error_mean_P_abs P_abs (mean(P_sim) − mean(P_ref)) / |mean(P_ref)| (signed means: Pabs = Pd + Ps can be negative) — error_min_{tag} f_pto, P_abs min(sim) − min(ref) same as signal error_max_{tag} f_pto, P_abs max(sim) − max(ref) same as signal peak_error_{tag} x, xdot, f_pto, P_abs Mean positive-peak value of sim minus mean positive-peak value of ref same as signal dist_mean_error_{tag} x, xdot, f_pto, P_abs mean(sim − ref) — signed bias same as signal dist_mae_{tag} x, xdot, f_pto, P_abs mean(|sim − ref|) — mean absolute error same as signal dist_std_{tag} x, xdot, f_pto, P_abs std(sim − ref) — error standard deviation same as signal dist_var_{tag} x, xdot, f_pto, P_abs var(sim − ref) — error variance same as signal² phase_lag_s_{tag} x, xdot Lag [s] at peak of cross-correlation between sim and ref s corr_peak_{tag} x, xdot Peak cross-correlation coefficient (−1 to 1) — phase_mean_deg_{tag} x, xdot Mean instantaneous phase difference (Hilbert-based) deg phase_std_deg_{tag} x, xdot Std of instantaneous phase difference deg time_ratio — physical_duration / wall_clock_time — solver speed relative to real time —

Saved per case to metric/scalar_<group>.csv, rows = models.

docs.title: Statistical summary (model_stats.csv)
docs.text:
After all cases are computed, every scalar metric above is aggregated across cases per model. Four summary columns are written for each metric key:

Suffix Definition {metric}_mean Mean across cases {metric}_std Standard deviation across cases {metric}_min Minimum across cases {metric}_max Maximum across cases

Example columns: nrmse_range_x_mean, nrmse_range_x_std, rel_error_mean_P_abs_mean, time_ratio_mean, …

Rows = models. Saved to metric/model_stats.csv.

docs.title: 1D outputs per case
docs.text:
These are not scalar metrics but are saved alongside them for plotting.

File Columns Description cross_corr_<group>.csv lag_s, ref_x, ref_xdot, {model}_x, {model}_xdot Normalised cross-correlation vs lag for each model inst_phase_<group>.csv t, {model}_x_deg, {model}_xdot_deg Instantaneous phase difference [deg] vs time

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
nrmse_range vs nrmse_true: range-normalised NRMSE is the default because it is bounded and insensitive to DC offset. True-normalised collapses when the reference RMS is small (near-zero mean signals) — avoid it for P_abs.

time_ratio: values > 1 mean the solver runs faster than real time. Read from the time_ratio column written by run_validate.

peak_error: uses scipy.find_peaks on the raw (un-smoothed) signal. Unreliable for irregular wave cases with many small peaks — treat as indicative only.

phase_lag_s / corr_peak: computed from normalised cross-correlation over the full clipped window. Phase lag is positive when the model leads the reference.

phase_mean_deg / phase_std_deg: Hilbert-transform-based instantaneous phase difference. Meaningful only for near-monochromatic signals (regular waves); interpret with caution for irregular seas.

docs.title: Model
docs.text:
Defines the body, the type and the force terms of a 1-DOF (heave) model. Consumed by run_validate and run_identify.

Model files model.json live in source/models/<name>/.

docs.title: JSON config
docs.text:
This is an example of model.json for a linear WEC (linear restoring, radiation state space, Froude-Krylov and diffraction convolution) with the PTO gains of the CFD case.

{
  "name": "lin",
  "type": "physics",
  "description": "Linear",
  "body": {
    "hydro_sphere_pkl": "r5_m40",
    "rho": 1025,
    "g": 9.81
  },
  "force_terms": {
    "restoring": "linear",
    "radiation": "state_space",
    "fk": "linear_conv",
    "diffraction": "linear_conv",
    "pressure_field": null,
    "drag": null,
    "pto": {"stiffness": "cfd", "damping": "cfd"}
  }
}
Field Type Required Description name string Yes Model name, normally the folder name containing model.json (not checked) type string Yes Model type. Only "physics" for now (data-based types will be added) description string No Free text body dict Yes hydro_sphere_pkl: name of the HydroSphere pickle in source/models/bem/<name>/ (BEM data, mass, radius, stiffness, water depth, panel mesh). rho, g: physical constants force_terms dict Yes Composable force model — see force_terms identified dict With drag: "viscous" Parameters written by run_identify (c_v, method, metric, …)

The equation of motion is \((m + m_\infty)\,\ddot{x} = \sum F\), with \(m\) the body mass and \(m_\infty\) the infinite-frequency added mass (only with a radiation state_space term).

docs.title: force_terms
docs.text:
Seven categories, all keys required, each holding at most one term: null means no term. A missing or unknown key is an error.

Key Physics restoring Static (hydrostatic) pressure, including gravity radiation Radiation damping and added mass fk Froude-Krylov: dynamic pressure of the incident wave diffraction Scattered wave (linear) pressure_field Static + dynamic incident pressure in one panel integration (full nonlinear Froude-Krylov) drag Viscous drag pto Power take-off

A term is written as a string, or as a dict {"type": ..., <parameters>} when it takes parameters. Any category can also be prescribed from the CFD. The full linear excitation is fk linear_conv + diffraction linear_conv.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Wave components \((A, \omega, k, \varphi)\), waves along +x, x = 0 at the buoy centre (reference wave gauge position): \(\eta(x, t) = \sum A \cos(\omega t - k x + \varphi)\). They come from the reconstructed wave elevation of the handled CFD case (_wave_recon.csv) or directly from the generated synthetic wave.
  • Water depth \(h\) is the BEM depth of the HydroSphere. \(k\) follows the dispersion relation \(\omega^2 = g k \tanh(k h)\) (\(k = \omega^2 / g\) in deep water).
  • Wetted surface is always determined using the true wave: the measured η(t) for flat terms, the recomposed wave with all components for _x terms.
  • Dynamic pressure is determined using the n_wave_components largest components of the wave ("all" for every component).
  • Wheeler stretching in every dynamic pressure: the depth profile is evaluated at the stretched coordinate \(z_s = h (z - \eta) / (h + \eta)\), \(\cosh(k (z_s + h)) / \cosh(k h)\) (\(e^{k (z - \eta)}\) in deep water). The dynamic pressure equals \(\rho g \eta\) at the surface and never grows above it.

docs.title: restoring
docs.text:
Static pressure, gravity included.

Option Free surface over the body Pressure Method Interpolation key Column "linear" — (mean surface) linearised: F = −K·x analytic — fhs_lin "nonlinear" η = 0 (still water) F = ρg·V_sub(x) − mg analytic (spherical cap) — fhs_nl "nonlinear_eta" flat η(t), measured F = ρg·V_sub(x, η) − mg, corresponds to p(z=η)=0 analytic restoring fhs_nl_eta "nonlinear_eta_z0" flat η(t), measured F = ρg·(V_sub − η·A_WP) − mg, from divergence theorem with p(z=0)=0 (Giorgi) analytic restoring fhs_nl_eta_z0 "nonlinear_eta_x" η(x, t), recomposed p = ρg·(η(x_c, t) − z), corresponds to p(z=η)=0 panels — fhs_nl_eta_x "nonlinear_eta_z0_x" η(x, t), recomposed p = −ρg·z, corresponds to p(z=0)=0 panels — fhs_nl_eta_z0_x

V_sub: submerged volume below the free surface. A_WP: waterplane area at the free-surface height. K = ρg·πr².

docs.title: radiation
docs.text: Option Formula Method Columns "state_space" F = −(Cr·z + Dr·ẋ), matrices from HydroSphere, added mass ma_inf folded into the left-hand side (m + ma_inf)·ẍ state space, radiation states z integrated with the body fr_damp (damping/memory part), fr_lin = fr_damp − ma_inf·ẍ (total, output only)

docs.title: fk
docs.text:
Froude-Krylov: dynamic incident-wave pressure only. The static part is the restoring term.

Option Free surface (mask + Wheeler) Dynamic pressure Method Parameters Interpolation key Column "linear_conv" — (mean surface, linear BEM) linear FK force: IRF ∗ η convolution, FK IRF from HydroSphere — excitation f_fk_lin "nonlinear" flat η(t), measured ρg·Σ A·f_k(z)·cos(ωt + φ) panels n_wave_components excitation f_fk_nl "nonlinear_x" η(x, t), recomposed ρg·Σ A·f_k(z)·cos(ωt − kx + φ) panels n_wave_components — f_fk_nl_x

f_k(z): depth profile with Wheeler stretching (see Conventions). Example: "fk": {"type": "nonlinear_x", "n_wave_components": 30}.

docs.title: diffraction
docs.text:
Option Formula Method Interpolation key Column "linear_conv" linear diffraction force: IRF ∗ η convolution, diffraction IRF from HydroSphere excitation fd_lin

The nonlinear FK terms (fk nonlinear*, pressure_field) contain no diffraction: add "diffraction": "linear_conv" for the scattered wave.

docs.title: pressure_field
docs.text:
Full incident pressure (static (p(z=0)=0) + dynamic) integrated in one panel pass, as in Giorgi's NLFK. The static and dynamic parts are still saved as two separate columns. The static column includes gravity, so no restoring term is needed with it.

Option Free surface Pressure Method Parameters Interpolation key Columns "airy" flat η(t), measured −ρg·z + ρg·Σ A·f_k(z)·cos(ωt + φ) panels n_wave_components excitation fhs_nl_eta_z0 + f_fk_nl "airy_x" η(x, t), recomposed −ρg·z + ρg·Σ A·f_k(z)·cos(ωt − kx + φ) panels n_wave_components — fhs_nl_eta_z0_x + f_fk_nl_x

airy_x gives exactly nonlinear_eta_z0_x + fk nonlinear_x, in one loop instead of two. airy differs from nonlinear_eta_z0 + fk nonlinear only by the panel error of the static part (analytic in nonlinear_eta_z0).

n_wave_components: number of largest-amplitude wave components used for the dynamic pressure (positive integer or "all"). Lever on computation time.

docs.title: drag
docs.text: Option Formula Requires Column "viscous" F = −c_v·|ẋ|·ẋ (Morison-type) identified.c_v (from run_identify, scheme viscous_drag) f_visc

docs.title: pto
docs.text:
Option Formula Columns {"stiffness": k, "damping": b} F = −k·x − b·ẋ, with numbers [N/m], [N·s/m] fs_pto, fd_pto, fpto {"stiffness": "cfd", "damping": "cfd"} same, with the gains of the CFD case (one or both keys) fs_pto, fd_pto, fpto {"type": "cfd", "force": <column>} PTO force prescribed from the CFD cfd_<column>, fpto null no PTO —

"cfd" gains need a CFD case with a body: an error for synthetic waves and wave-only cases (empty basin). Synthetic models use numeric gains; their values appear in the synthetic CSV names (_d<damping>_k<stiffness>). In run_identify pi_gain, the optimised gains replace the model's PTO.

docs.title: CFD-prescribed forces
docs.text: Any category can be replaced by a force column of the CFD case, read as a time series: {"type": "cfd", "force": <column>}, e.g. "restoring": {"type": "cfd", "force": "ftot"}. The column is saved as cfd_<column> and feeds the role of its category. pressure_field takes {"type": "cfd", "static_force": ..., "dynamic_force": ...} (one or both). A prescribed radiation has no states (left-hand side mass m). Needs a CFD case with that column (error for synthetic waves). Interpolation key cfd.

docs.title: Role columns
docs.text:
Every model also writes generic role columns, with the same name in every model (zeros if the category is absent), so models and CFD can be compared by name:

Column Definition F_static static force (incl. −m·g): restoring, static part of pressure_field F_exc excitation: fk + diffraction, dynamic part of pressure_field F_rad total radiation (= fr_lin) F_drag viscous drag F_hyd total fluid force = F_static + m·g (if static present) + F_exc + F_rad + F_drag, comparable to the CFD fhyd_cfd fpto total PTO force

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: Time margins — t_warmup and t_causal are derived automatically from the model and BEM data and are not JSON inputs. Radiation state_space: t_warmup = 30 s. fk or diffraction linear_conv: t_warmup = t_irf end, t_causal = |t_irf start|. Panel terms need no margin. The largest values across the models of a run are applied to every simulation.

docs.title: Pipeline Overview
docs.text: HIVE is built around pipelines ran via scripts, each driven by a JSON input file and writing outputs to a structured folder. The core chain is run_handle_data → run_validate → run_metric, with run_identify to build new models.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Script What it does Config location Output location run_handle_data Reads raw CFD time series, applies cut times and optional resampling, computes wave parameters, decomposes the wave and computes hydrodynamic quantities, saves one processed dataset per case inputs/handle_case/<name>.json data/handled/<name>/ run_validate Loads processed datasets (or generates synthetic waves) and model.json files, runs the forward simulations via SimRun and saves the simulated time series. No metric, no plot inputs/validate_case/<name>.json out/validated_case/<name>/ run_metric Reloads a run_validate output folder, computes all metrics against the CFD or a model reference, and makes the time series and metric plots inputs/metric_case/<name>.json out/validated_case/<validated_case>/ (metric/, plots/) run_identify Uses a scheme module (viscous_drag or pi_gain) to identify model parameters from CFD data or synthetic waves, writes the identified model.json (viscous drag) and the results inputs/identify_case/<name>.json out/identified_case/<name>/

Each script reads the input .json file given by the --case <name>.json argument. The stem of that filename becomes the output folder name — choose stems that are short, lowercase, and use underscores.

All input files are strict: every key must be present (null means "none"), and a missing or unknown key stops the script with an error. There are no silent defaults.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
The outputs are data (.csv), metrics (.csv), results (.json) and plots (.png and .pkl). Every plot is saved as both .png (for quick viewing) and .pkl (interactive Matplotlib figure). Reload a .pkl interactively with the "load saved figures" option at the rerun prompt, or directly:

import pickle, matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig = pickle.load(open("plots/spectrum.pkl", "rb"))
plt.show()

Every script also writes a copy of its input config and a run.log (metric.log for run_metric) next to its outputs.

docs.title: run_handle_data
docs.text: Processes raw CFD time series into a standardised format ready for validation and identification. Wave-only datasets (empty wave basin, no body) can be processed too.

docs.title: first run
docs.text:
python -m script.run_handle_data --case <name>.json

Config files .json live in inputs/handle_case/. The filename stem becomes the output folder name under data/handled/.

docs.title: rerun options
docs.text:
When the output folder already exists, the script prompts:

[1] erase and redo all     — reprocess + replot from scratch
[2] stop, do nothing
[3] load saved figures     — reopen existing .pkl plots interactively
[4] remake figures only    — reuse processed CSVs, regenerate plots

Option [4] is useful when tuning plot parameters without reprocessing data.

docs.title: what it does
docs.text:
1. Reads each case folder from data/cfd/
  2. Instantiates a DataHandle object per case
  3. Calls processData() — computes the wave parameters (spectrum, \(H_s\), \(T_e\), energy flux, depth type, wave length) and, for a case with a body, the PTO force and absorbed power, the hydrostatic forces, the linear excitation force (fe_lin and its Froude-Krylov / diffraction parts) and the radiation force
  4. Optionally resamples to a target dt
  5. Decomposes the measured wave elevation into components \((A, \omega, k, \varphi)\) on the final time grid (energy band wave_energy_fraction), and saves the recomposed elevation eta_rec
  6. For a case with a body: computes the panel forces from the CFD motion and the recomposed wave (fhs_nl_eta_x, fhs_nl_eta_z0_x, f_fk_nl_x), with the same force classes as the models
  7. Saves processed data, wave parameters and wave components to data/handled/<name>/data/
  8. Generates and saves plots to data/handled/<name>/plots/

docs.title: Input JSON config
docs.text:
{
  "wave_type": "irr",
  "cut_time": [30, 0],
  "duration": null,
  "hydro_sphere_pkl": "r5_m40",
  "dt": 0.05,
  "water_depth": 60,
  "wave_energy_fraction": 0.999,
  "n_wave_components": 100,
  "cases": [
    {
      "T": 6.5,
      "H": 2.0,
      "damping": 120000,
      "stiffness": -430000,
      "tag": "example",
      "plot": true
    }
  ],
  "plot_options": {
    "sea_state": true,
    "power": true,
    "dynamics": true,
    "hydro": true,
    "3d": true,
    "variable": ["fe_lin", "x"]
  }
}

All fields are required.

Field Type Description wave_type "irr" | "reg" Wave type used in the CFD simulation cut_time [float, float] Seconds to discard from [start, end] of the raw signal. Use 0 to keep to the edge duration float | null Maximum duration (s) to retain after the start cut. null keeps all remaining data hydro_sphere_pkl string Name of the BEM pickle source/models/bem/<name>/<name>.pkl, e.g. "r5_m40" dt float | null Target resampling timestep (s). null keeps the original CFD timestep water_depth float | "deep" Water depth of the CFD case (m). Used for the dispersion relation, depth type, wave length and energy flux. A warning is printed when it differs from the BEM depth of the HydroSphere (the models use the BEM depth) wave_energy_fraction float Energy fraction kept by the wave decomposition (frequency band around the peak), e.g. 0.999 n_wave_components int | "all" Number of largest wave components used for the dynamic pressure of the CFD-side panel force f_fk_nl_x cases list[dict] List of cases to process (see cases) plot_options dict Controls which plots are generated (see plot_options)

docs.title: cases
docs.text:
Each entry in cases:

Field Type Required Description T float yes Wave period from the CFD folder name (s), written as a float (10.0, not 10) H float yes Wave height from the CFD folder name (m) damping int | null yes PTO damping coefficient (N·s/m). null for a wave-only case stiffness int | null yes PTO stiffness coefficient (N/m). Use negative for spring-like reactive control. null for a wave-only case tag string | null no Optional suffix appended to the CFD folder name and output label plot bool no Whether to include this case in plots. Default: true

The case folder read in data/cfd/ is out_Case_<T>_<H>[_<damping>_<stiffness>][_<tag>], with T and H written without the dot (e.g. out_Case_65_20_120000_-430000_example, out_Case_66_20_emptybasin).

Each case is assigned a label, built from the measured \(H_s\) and \(T_e\) and the case parameters. The label is used as the series label in plots and as the group name in run_validate and run_metric:

Hs{Hs}p{dec}_Te{Te}p{dec}[_d{damping}_k{stiffness}][_{tag}]

Example: Hs2p2_Te6p6_d120000_k-430000_example. The processed CSV files are named after the nominal H and T of the config instead (e.g. Hs2p0_Te6p5_d120000_k-430000_example_data.csv).

docs.text:

docs.title: run_identify
docs.text: Identifies model parameters from CFD reference data or synthetic waves, using a pluggable scheme system.

docs.title: first run
docs.text:
python -m script.run_identify --case <name>.json

Config files <name>.json live in inputs/identify_case/. The filename stem becomes the output folder name under out/identified_case/.

docs.title: rerun options
docs.text:
When the output folder already exists, the script prompts:

[1] erase and redo
[2] stop, do nothing
[3] load saved figures     — reopen existing .pkl plots interactively
[4] save with date suffix  — run and save under <name>_YYYYMMDD (keeps existing folder)

Option [4] is useful to keep previous identification results while running a new one with the same JSON input.

docs.title: available schemes
docs.text: Scheme Description Note "viscous_drag" identify a viscous drag coefficient given a base model to fit CFD reference data see Scheme: viscous_drag "pi_gain" find optimal PI gains (PTO stiffness and damping) per sea state to maximize or minimize an objective, absorbed power for instance see Scheme: pi_gain

docs.title: what it does
docs.text:
Runs an optimization depending on the chosen identification scheme and based on a chosen model. More explicitly:

  1. Loads the base model definition from source/models/<base_model>/model.json and its HydroSphere
  2. Creates a DDFeed — loads the training waves (handled CFD cases or synthetic waves at the BEM water depth) and runs scheme.prep()
  3. Creates an Optimizer — owns the simulation helpers and delegates to scheme.run()
  4. Computes time margins (t_warmup, t_causal) from the base model and BEM data
  5. Saves the identified model (viscous drag), result JSON, data CSVs and plots to out/identified_case/<name>/

docs.title: Scheme: viscous_drag
docs.text:
Identifies the quadratic drag coefficient \(c_v\) in \(f_{visc} = -c_v |\dot{x}| \dot{x}\) for:

  • per-case — \(c_v\) fitted independently to each wave case
  • global — single \(c_v\) fitted across all cases pooled together → corresponds to the model output written to model.json

docs.text:
{
  "scheme": "viscous_drag",
  "waves_train": ["test_0_handle_case"],
  "base_model": "lin",
  "scheme_params": {
    "type": ["force", "response"],
    "search": ["opt", "grid"],
    "base_force": "fhyd_lin",
    "c_v_min": 0,
    "c_v_max": 150000,
    "n_points": 10,
    "objective": "rmse_x"
  },
  "solver": {
    "method": "RK4",
    "dt": 0.05,
    "interpolation": {"restoring": "linear", "excitation": "linear", "cfd": "linear"}
  },
  "plot_options": {}
}

docs.title: scheme_params
docs.text:
All fields are required.

Field Type Options / values Multiple entry (list) Description type string "force", "response" Yes Identification type. "force" fits \(c_v\) to match \(F_{hyd}\) ; "response" fits \(c_v\) to match the motion (objective on the simulated response) search string "opt", "grid" Yes Search method. "opt" uses a bounded scalar optimiser on \([c_{v,min}, c_{v,max}]\) ; "grid" sweeps a uniform grid over the same range base_force string any column present in the handled dataset No Force column \(f_{col}\) of the base model evaluated on the CFD motion, used by type = "force": \(f_{hyd,cfd} = f_{col} + f_{visc}\). Only fhyd_lin (linear model) exists in the handled data c_v_min float non-negative [N·s²/m²] No Lower bound of the \(c_v\) search range. 0 ≤ c_v_min < c_v_max is checked c_v_max float positive [N·s²/m²] No Upper bound of the \(c_v\) search range n_points int any positive integer No Grid resolution — used only when search = "grid" objective string Any available metric, e.g. "rmse_x" No Metric used to score \(c_v\) candidates

The four possible type × search method combinations are: force_opt, force_grid, response_opt, response_grid. Pass lists to run several at once. The model.json is written with the global \(c_v\) of the best method (lowest objective).

docs.title: waves_train
docs.text:
CFD case — {"type": "cfd_case", "case_name": <handled folder under data/handled/>}. Every case of the folder is used, including wave-only cases (empty basin): only the wave elevation and its components are needed.

Synthetic wave — same keys as in run_validate, all required:

Field Type Description type "synthetic" Wave generated as a sum of regular components wave_type "reg" · "irr" Regular sinusoid or irregular JONSWAP T float Wave period (regular) or energy period (irregular) [s] H float Wave height (regular) or significant wave height (irregular) [m] gamma float | null JONSWAP peak enhancement factor (null for regular) duration float Signal duration [s] dw float Frequency step of the components [rad/s] w_end float Highest component frequency [rad/s] wave_energy_fraction float Energy fraction of the components kept around the peak

The synthetic wave is generated at the solver dt, at the BEM water depth of the base model.

docs.title: scheme_params fields
docs.text:
Field Type Default Options / values Multiple entry (list) Description method string "opt" "analytical" (complex-conjugate gains from linear potential flow, HydroSphere.pi_gain(Te), does not consider bounds) · "opt" using an optimizer · "grid" doing a grid-search · or a list of several Yes Identification method(s). Pass a list to run and compare multiple methods in one execution B_min float 0.0 any float [N·s/m] No Lower bound for \(B_{pto}\) search B_max float 1e6 any float [N·s/m] No Upper bound for \(B_{pto}\) search K_min float -1e6 any float [N/m] No Lower bound for \(K_{pto}\) search K_max float 1e6 any float [N/m] No Upper bound for \(K_{pto}\) search n_B int 20 any positive integer No Grid points along \(B\) axis — used only when method = "grid" n_K int 20 any positive integer No Grid points along \(K\) axis — used only when method = "grid" B_init float midpoint of [B_min, B_max] any float [N·s/m] No Initial value for the "opt" optimiser K_init float midpoint of [K_min, K_max] any float [N/m] No Initial value for the "opt" optimiser objective dict {"name": "mean_P_abs", "direction": "maximize"} see Metric for "name", "maximize" or "minimize" for "direction" No Metric used to score \((B, K)\) candidates stability dict {"enabled": false, "r": 5.0} enabled: true / false · r: float (m) No Early-stop check: aborts integration if ( n_jobs int 1 any integer · -1 = all CPU cores No Parallel workers for "grid" search via joblib

The "analytical" method is based on linear potential flow theory and hence limited to regular waves. For irregular waves the energy period is used.

docs.title: run_metric
docs.text: Computes all metrics and makes all plots (time series and metrics) from a finished run_validate output folder. No simulation is run: the simulated CSVs are reloaded.

docs.title: first run
docs.text:
python -m script.run_metric --case <name>.json

Config files <name>.json live in inputs/metric_case/. The outputs are written into the validated case folder out/validated_case/<validated_case>/.

docs.title: rerun options
docs.text:
When metric results already exist in that folder, the script prompts:

[1] erase and rerun (metrics + plots)
[2] load existing plots
[3] stop, do nothing

docs.title: what it does
docs.text:
1. Reads the copy of the run_validate config (models, wave sources, solvers) in out/validated_case/<validated_case>/
  2. Reloads the simulated time series of every (wave, model, solver) run and the CFD reference cases
  3. Sets the metric reference: the CFD case, or the simulation of one model and solver
  4. Computes all metrics on the valid time window (time margins as in run_validate for a CFD reference; model simulations are already clipped)
  5. Saves the metric CSVs to metric/ and the plots to plots/

docs.title: Input JSON config
docs.text:
{
  "validated_case": "test_4_dt",
  "plot_options": {
    "states": true,
    "forces": true,
    "variable": [],
    "metrics": true
  },
  "reference": {"model": "lin_syn", "solver": "RK4 0.01 linlinlin"}
}

All fields are required, and unknown keys are errors.

Field Type Description validated_case string Name of the run_validate config (= output folder under out/validated_case/) plot_options dict Plots to make. See plot_options reference "cfd" | dict Metric reference. "cfd": the CFD case. {"model": <model name>, "solver": "<method> <dt> <interp>"}: the simulation of that model with that solver, written as in the run label (e.g. "RK4 0.05 linlinlin"); it is removed from the compared models

The reference only affects the metrics: the time series plots always show the CFD (when it has a body) and all models.

A model reference is needed for synthetic waves (no CFD data) and for wave-only CFD cases (empty basin: no body motion). "cfd" with a wave-only case stops with an error.

docs.title: run_validate
docs.text: Runs models against CFD reference data or synthetic wave signals for all (model, wave source, solver) combinations, and saves the simulated time series. Metrics and plots are made afterwards by run_metric on this output folder.

docs.title: first run
docs.text:
python -m script.run_validate --case <name>.json

Config files <name>.json live in inputs/validate_case/. The filename stem becomes the output folder name under out/validated_case/.

docs.title: rerun options
docs.text:
When the output folder already exists, the script prompts:

[1] erase and redo all     — also erases the run_metric results and plots of this folder
[2] stop, do nothing

docs.title: what it does
docs.text:
Runs all (model, wave source, solver) combinations. More explicitly:

  1. Loads all model definitions from source/models/<name>/model.json and their HydroSphere
  2. Resolves wave sources — loads the handled CFD cases or generates the synthetic waves (water depth: BEM depth of the models). A warning is printed when the CFD case depth differs from the BEM depth
  3. Checks the solver dt against the CFD reference dt; prompts to continue if they differ
  4. Computes the time margins (t_warmup, t_causal) of every model, and applies the largest to all runs
  5. Runs the full record for every combination, then clips it to the valid time window
  6. Saves the time-series CSVs, the synthetic waves and a copy of each model to out/validated_case/<name>/

A run that fails (e.g. diverges) is logged with its error and the others continue.

docs.text:
{
  "models": [
    {"name": "lin"},
    {"name": "nlfk_x"}
  ],
  "wave_sources": [
    {"type": "cfd_case", "case_name": "test_0_handle_case"},
    {
      "type": "synthetic",
      "wave_type": "irr",
      "T": 6.5,
      "H": 2.0,
      "gamma": 3.3,
      "duration": 150,
      "dw": 0.01,
      "w_end": 8.0,
      "wave_energy_fraction": 0.999
    }
  ],
  "solvers": [
    {"method": "RK4", "dt": 0.05, "interpolation": {"restoring": "linear", "excitation": "linear", "cfd": "linear"}}
  ],
  "eta_inputs": [{"type": "true"}],
  "simulation": [{"type": "closed_loop"}]
}

All fields are required, and unknown keys are errors.

Field Type Multiple entry (list) Description models dict Yes. All entries are simulated Models to validate. Each dict has exactly a "name" key pointing to a folder under source/models/. See Model wave_sources dict Yes. All entries are loaded and run independently Wave elevation sources. See wave_sources solvers dict Yes. All entries are run for every (model, wave) pair Simulation solver settings. See Solver. Two solvers with the same method, dt and interpolation are an error eta_inputs dict Yes Wave elevation given to the model. Only {"type": "true"} (the measured or generated elevation) is implemented simulation dict Yes Simulation type. Only {"type": "closed_loop"} is implemented

All models × wave_sources × solvers combinations are run automatically. Pass lists to any of the three fields to expand the matrix.

docs.title: wave_sources
docs.text:
CFD case — {"type": "cfd_case", "case_name": ...}

Field Type Description type "cfd_case" Wave elevation and reference data from a handled case case_name string Handled data folder name under data/handled/. Every case of the folder is run

The simulation starts from the CFD state at the first time step. A wave-only case (empty basin) starts from rest, and its models need numeric PTO gains.

Synthetic wave — {"type": "synthetic", ...}

Field Type Options / values Description type "synthetic" — Wave generated as a sum of regular components. No reference data: only the model responses are produced wave_type string "reg" · "irr" (JONSWAP) Wave type T float s Wave period (regular) or energy period (irregular) H float m Wave height (regular) or significant wave height (irregular) gamma float | null — JONSWAP peak enhancement factor (null for a regular wave) duration float s Signal duration dw float rad/s Frequency step of the components w_end float rad/s Highest component frequency wave_energy_fraction float — Energy fraction of the components kept around the peak

A synthetic wave has no time step of its own: it is generated once from its components and evaluated on each solver grid, so every solver sees the same wave (a warning is printed if components exceed the Nyquist frequency \(\pi / dt\)). The wave water depth is the BEM depth of the models. The PTO gains come from each model (a synthetic wave has no CFD gains, so "cfd" PTO gains are an error).

docs.title: naming
docs.text:
• run label: <model> | <method> <dt> <interp>, where <interp> gives the interpolation of restoring, excitation and cfd as lin / cub / nul (e.g. lin | RK4 0.05 linlinlin)
  • group: the CFD case label (e.g. Hs2p2_Te6p6_d120000_k-430000_example), or synthetic_<wave_type>_Hs<H>_Te<T> for a synthetic wave
  • CSV: <group>_<label>.csv with the label made file-safe, e.g. Hs2p2_Te6p6_d120000_k-430000_example_lin_RK4_0_05_linlinlin.csv. For a synthetic wave, the group is followed by the PTO gains of the model, _d<damping>_k<stiffness> (_d0_k0 without PTO), e.g. synthetic_irr_Hs2p0_Te6p5_d120000_k0_lin_syn_RK4_0_05_linlinlin.csv

docs.title: time series (data/*.csv)
docs.text:
Every column is on the solver time grid, clipped to the valid window. The model columns depend on its force terms (see Model):

Column Units Description t s Time x, xdot m, m/s Displacement and velocity eta m Wave elevation specific columns N One column per force term, e.g. fhs_lin, fr_damp, f_fk_lin, fd_lin, f_fk_nl_x, f_visc, cfd_<column> fr_lin N Total radiation force (fr_damp − ma_inf·ẍ), with a radiation term F_static, F_exc, F_rad, F_drag N Role columns, same name in every model (zeros if the category is absent) F_hyd N Total fluid force, comparable to the CFD fhyd_cfd fs_pto, fd_pto, fpto N PTO spring, damper and total force Pabs, Pd, Ps W Absorbed, damper and spring power sim_time s Wall-clock integration time (constant column) time_ratio — Simulated physical time / sim_time (constant column)

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
Time margins — t_warmup (start) and t_causal (end) are derived from the model definitions and BEM data, not JSON inputs. Radiation state_space: 30 s warmup (states start at 0). Linear convolution (fk or diffraction linear_conv): t_irf[-1] warmup and |t_irf[0]| causal (±30 s with the F2T IRF). The largest margins across the models of a run are applied to every simulation, so all models are compared on the same window. time_ratio uses the full simulated duration.

dt mismatch — if a solver dt differs from the CFD reference dt, the script warns and asks to continue. The metrics are computed on the coarser of the two grids.

docs.title: Solver
docs.text: Documents the solver entry used in run_validate (solvers list) and run_identify (solver) configs.

docs.title: input JSON config
docs.text:
{
  "method": "RK4",
  "dt": 0.05,
  "interpolation": {
    "restoring": "linear",
    "excitation": "linear",
    "cfd": "linear"
  }
}

All fields are required.

Field Type Options / values Description method string "euler", "rk2", "rk4" (any case) Fixed-step integration method dt float any positive float (s) Fixed timestep interpolation dict keys "restoring", "excitation", "cfd", all required — values "linear", "cubic", null How measured inputs are read inside a time step. See interpolation

In run_validate, the solver appears in the run label and the CSV name as <method> <dt> <interp>, with the three interpolation options as lin / cub / nul in the order restoring, excitation, cfd (e.g. RK4 0.05 linlinlin). Two solvers with the same method, dt and interpolation are an error.

docs.title: Interpolation options
docs.text:
For force terms driven by a measured time series, "linear" or "cubic" interpolates the input at each RK sub-stage time, and null freezes it at the start of the step. Post-processing always interpolates.

Key Terms Input restoring restoring: nonlinear_eta, nonlinear_eta_z0 measured η(t) excitation fk / diffraction: linear_conv precomputed f_fk_lin / fd_lin series excitation fk: nonlinear; pressure_field: airy measured η(t) for the wetted panels and Wheeler stretching (the wave phase always uses the exact time) cfd any {"type": "cfd", ...} term prescribed CFD columns

Each key covers one family of sampled inputs. The input is interpolated, then the term computes its force from it as usual.

restoring — measured η(t) in the nonlinear static force

Term What is interpolated How it is used restoring: nonlinear_eta measured η at the reference gauge submerged volume of the sphere below the flat surface at height η: \(F = \rho g V_{sub}(x, \eta) - m g\) restoring: nonlinear_eta_z0 same Giorgi form: \(F = \rho g (V_{sub} - \eta A_{WP}) - m g\)

excitation — the wave excitation inputs

Term What is interpolated How it is used fk: linear_conv the series f_fk_lin, computed once before the simulation by convolving η with the FK IRF (fe_conv) the force is read directly from the series diffraction: linear_conv the series fd_lin (η convolved with the diffraction IRF) same fk: nonlinear measured η, only for the free-surface height η sets which panels are wetted (below the flat surface) and the Wheeler stretching of the pressure profile. The dynamic pressure itself, \(\rho g \sum A f_k(z) \cos(\omega t + \varphi)\), is computed from the wave components at the exact time: it needs no interpolation pressure_field: airy measured η, same role same as fk nonlinear, for the static + dynamic pressure integrated together

cfd — prescribed CFD forces

Term What is interpolated How it is used any {"type": "cfd", "force": <column>} (and pressure_field static_force / dynamic_force) the CFD column (e.g. ftot, fpto, fhd_lin_r) the force is read directly from the column

Terms with no key — they read no sampled input:

Term Why restoring: linear, nonlinear depend only on the body position \(x\) radiation: state_space depends on the body velocity and the radiation states, integrated by the solver drag: viscous, pto gains depend only on the body state _x terms (nonlinear_eta_z0_x, nonlinear_eta_x, fk nonlinear_x, pressure_field airy_x) the wave η(x, t) and the pressure are rebuilt from the wave components at the exact time, so there are no samples to interpolate between

All other terms depend only on the state, or evaluate the wave components analytically (_x terms), and need no key.

Order of accuracy. Linear interpolation limits RK4 to second order, because the middle stages read the inputs between samples. Cubic interpolation gives fourth order back. null is first order.
